title: Customer Onboarding: Deployment Readiness & Risk Checklist (Private Deploys)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document is a pragmatic, step-by-step readiness and risk checklist for onboarding customers to Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It summarizes technical prerequisites, operational handoffs, acceptance criteria, and risk mitigations required before production cutover. Use this checklist during pre-engagement, staging validation, and final go/no-go reviews.

Scope
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed compute, and fully on-prem packages).
- Focuses on readiness gates: network, security, capacity, observability, upgrade/rollback preparedness, and contractual SLAs.

Owners & Roles
- Customer Success (CS): overall onboarding program owner, coordinates sign-offs.
- Deployment Engineering: provisioning, manifests, and day-2 automation.
- Security & Compliance: controls review and final evidence.
- SRE / Runtime Team: SLO definitions, alerting, and oncall runbook handoff.
- Customer: network, KMS, and compute environment ownership.

High-level Onboarding Phases (timeline expectation: 3–8 weeks depending on scope)
1) Pre-engagement (1 week): intake questionnaire, initial gap analysis.
2) Staging & Integration (2–4 weeks): infra provisioning, config validation, smoke tests.
3) Hardening & QA (1–2 weeks): performance verification, reliability drills.
4) Cutover & Stabilization (1 week): production rollout, early life monitoring.

Readiness Gates (must be green to proceed)
- Gate 1 — Requirements & Contract: contract signed, data residency and confidentiality clauses in place, support SLAs agreed.
- Gate 2 — Network Connectivity: all required ports and routes validated, peering & firewall rules applied.
- Gate 3 — Compute & Storage: nodes provisioned, NVMe/SSD validated, GPU firmware/drivers pinned.
- Gate 4 — Security & Identity: KMS keys provisioned, RBAC mapped, SSO tested.
- Gate 5 — Observability & Alerting: Prometheus/Datadog endpoints validated, dashboard templates imported.
- Gate 6 — Upgrade & Rollback Plan: version locks, canary plan, rollback triggers documented.

Technical Checklist (detailed)
1) Network and DNS - Required outbound endpoints (control plane) allowed: control.redwood.ai:443, registry.redwood.ai:443
- Ports and routes table (example):
| Component | Protocol | Ports | Notes |
| Control plane API | HTTPS | 443 outbound | TLS 1.2+, allow SNI |
| Model pull (registry) | HTTPS | 443 outbound | CIDR allowlist optional |
| Inter-node runtime | gRPC / TCP | 22000-22015 | Overlay network for KV cache replication |
| Metrics | Prometheus | 9090 inbound (optional) | Pushgateway or scrape config |
- DNS: internal FQDNs provisioned (e.g., runtime-api.cluster.customer.local) and TTLs set to <=60s for fast failover.
- MTU and overlay note: minimum MTU 1400 recommended for RDMA over fabric clusters.

2) Compute & Storage - Node inventory: list of hosts with CPU, GPU, RAM, disk, driver versions. Example acceptance: all GPU nodes must report CUDA 12.0+ and driver >=535.
- Storage perf baseline: 2000 IOPS sustained for model artifacts or packaging may need local NVMe cache.
- Swap and OOM handling: swap disabled on inference nodes; OOM killer soft limits tuned.

3) Security & Identity - KMS/HSM integration: sample KMS ARN or endpoint validated.
- Secrets handling: runtime components must not store plaintext secrets; Vault or KMS must be used.
- RBAC matrix must be reviewed and signed by customer security. Example roles: deployer, ops, auditor.
- Audit logging: system audit logs routed to customer SIEM or Redwood log-forwarder.

4) Observability & Alerts - Metrics: token latency p50/p95, request success rate, model load failures.
- Traces: distributed tracing instrumented for API -> runtime paths.
- Alert thresholds (SRE recommended):
  - request_error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> page oncall
  - p95 latency > 2x SLO for 10m -> page oncall
  - model_load_failures >= 3 in 15m -> trigger rollback plan
- Dashboard templates: import instructions and sample Grafana URL.

5) Performance Acceptance Criteria - Throughput target: validated against customer's QPS and token length distribution.
- Example acceptance table:
| Workload | Target p95 latency | Min throughput | Test tool |
| Chat (<=512 tokens) | 350ms | 200 qps | loadtest-chat-v2 |
| Gen (<=2048 tokens) | 1.2s | 40 qps | loadtest-gen |

6) Upgrade & Rollback Preparedness - Version pinning: production manifests must pin model and runtime versions.
- Canary strategy: 5% traffic canary with automatic metrics comparison for 30 minutes.
- Rollback triggers (automated + manual):
  - Automated: error rate increased by 2x baseline OR p95 latency > 2x SLO for 10m.
  - Manual: customer product owner signs rollback after functional regressions.
- Rollback runbook snippet (example CLI):
  - # promote previous manifest
  - rwoodctl rollout promote --cluster prod --manifest manifests/prod-2026-01-15.yaml
  - # verify
  - rwoodctl health --cluster prod --check model_loads,latency,errors

Risk Matrix (summary)
- High risk: network misconfiguration (firewall / MTU), lack of KMS integration, insufficient GPU driver compatibility.
- Medium risk: missing observability hooks, under-provisioned local disk for model cache.
- Low risk: documentation gaps, role onboarding delays.

Mitigations
- Network pre-validation window: run a 48-hour connectivity test with control plane in staging. Capture PCAPs and traceroutes if intermittent.
- KMS dry-run: cryptographic challenge to ensure keys unwrap correctly and permission model works.
- Driver compatibility matrix: maintain a pinned matrix per model family in the onboarding ticket.

Operational Handover (must be delivered before cutover)
- Handover artifacts: runbooks, playbooks, SLO definitions, escalation contacts, oncall schedule.
- Known issues list: triage doc with current mitigations.
- Contact list: deployment engineering, SRE, CS manager, customer POC with timezones.

Final Go/No-Go Checklist (CS-led signoff)
1) Requirements & legal signoff: yes/no
2) Network smoke test: passed (attach logs)
3) Staging perf: met (attach perf-report-id)
4) Security review: signed checklist (attach evidence)
5) Observability: dashboards present, alerts wired
6) Upgrade/rollback tested and dry-run completed
7) Oncall handoff completed
8) Customer readiness (ops staff trained)

Post-cutover (first 72 hours) — Stabilization playbook
- Frequency: 15m cadence checks for first 12 hours, hourly checks until 72h.
- Focus: error rate, p95 latency, model availability, and cost anomalies.
- Escalation: if automated rollback triggers fire, deployment engineering and SRE join an incident bridge immediately.

Appendices
A) Example intake questionnaire (abbreviated)
- Preferred deployment mode: VPC / on-prem
- Primary region and network CIDRs
- KMS provider and key IDs
- Expected peak QPS and average token length
- Acceptable maintenance windows

B) Minimal CLI examples
- Validate connectivity:
  - curl -v https://control.redwood.ai/health --resolve "control.redwood.ai:443:203.0.113.10"
- List manifests on cluster:
  - rwoodctl manifests list --cluster staging

C) Evidence attachments checklist (for security/compliance)
- Network diagram (layer2/3)
- KMS integration test log
- Driver and firmware inventory CSV
- Performance report (staging)
- Signed SLO doc

Document maintenance
- Owner: Customer Success (Maya Chen)
- Review cadence: quarterly or triggered by major runtime release.
- Change log: track significant changes here.

Change log
- 2026-02-20: Added upgrade/rollback CLI snippet and tightened alert thresholds (Maya Chen).
- 2025-11-13: Initial published version (Maya Chen).

Related artifacts and links
- Onboarding ticket template: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/onboarding-ticket-template
- Runtime compatibility matrix: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/runtime-compat-matrix

If you are the CS lead for a new private deployment, duplicate this checklist into the onboarding ticket and attach evidence URLs.
